description: The AS externalized-name phrase — `[ AS literal-1 ]` on PROGRAM-ID (§2023:11.10.2 Formats 1 and 2), FUNCTION-ID (§2023:11.5.2 Formats 1 and 2), CLASS-ID (§2023:11.3.2), INTERFACE-ID (§2023:11.6.2), METHOD-ID (§2023:11.7.2) and the EXTERNAL clause (§2023:13.18.22.2, on a data description entry and on a file description entry alike — kb/Work PB511). §2023:8.3.2.2 2) gives it its meaning: the literal is the name externalized to the operating environment. X3.23-1985 has NO such phrase anywhere and AS is user-definable there (the user-word-as-2002 twin), so the whole phrase is a 2002 introduction. ONE grammar rule (externalizedNamePhrase) and ONE gate (VersionConformancePass ParseArm.VisitExternalizedNamePhrase) serve every site; below 2002 the gate names the edition (COBOL0900) instead of the bare syntax error the phrase drew before kb/Work PB303. The §2023:12.3.8.2 program-specifier shares the grammar rule and carries its own repository-program-2002 row for the specifier itself.
vcr: kb/Work PB303 — the phrase had no grammar surface at all: rejected 2002+ (COBOL0901, AS parsed as a user-defined word) and accepted at '85, the one edition where it does not exist
source:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
PROGRAM-ID. EXNQ1 AS "EXNQX".
PROCEDURE DIVISION.
MAIN.
    STOP RUN.
